correctness.rationale: Fermat's theorem and the curve equation give 90 rational smooth curve points (after excluding its unique geometric singular [1:1:1]); raw gradient differentiation yields projectively normalized tangent τ(Q)=[3/s−1/x:3/s−1/y:3/s−1/z]. Independent exhaustive arithmetic across all 133 rational plane points finds 72 distinct attained tangent coefficient lines and verifies the provided 18 are among them. Their line-incidence histogram is {1:90,2:15,3:25,7:3}, so all points are covered. Three explicit dual-side lines contain seven selected points each with three distinct selected pairwise vertices. The entire set of 72 attained tangents has incidence histogram {1:3,4:6,5:30,6:25,7:24,8:42,11:3}; no entire 12-point dual line lies in T. Thus any eligible covering subset is a nontrivial blocking set in PG(2,11), and Blokhuis's prime-order lower bound 3(p+1)/2=18 matches the construction. This is an exhaustive 133-point certificate plus an established published lower bound, not sample extrapolation.
